idea-plugin.name: Cobra torch
idea-plugin.description:
Tools for conda environment files named .conda_env.yml:
  • the conda icon instead of the YAML icon;
  • a toolbar above the editor: the environment's size (or "Conda env is not installed"), the computer (this one or the remote one), the NVIDIA GPU (model | VRAM | CUDA version), and buttons that run conda env update -f .conda_env.yml --prune, conda run --live-stream -n <name> jupyter lab and conda env remove -n <name>; a button opens the environment's folder in the file manager;
  • a click on the size lists every conda environment with its size and a remove button;
  • the installed version after each dependency that has none in the file, as a hint that is not part of the file;
  • a click on "This computer" connects to a remote computer over SSH (password, key or SSH agent; the key is found in ~/.ssh; the price per hour is asked, and the cost so far is shown): the toolbar then shows its environment, GPU and versions, and its buttons run there; JupyterLab opens here through an SSH tunnel; a click on "Remote computer" shows the connection and disconnects;
  • the official logo next to well-known dependencies (Python, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, Plotly, Jupyter, PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, ...) and the conda icon next to the conda-forge channel; a click opens the project's website;
  • the same logos next to imports in .py files and Jupyter notebooks;
  • a click on the GPU (or Tools | System Monitor) opens the System Monitor, for this computer or the connected remote one: each CPU's name, power and temperature and the load of each of its cores; the GPUs' name, power and temperature, then a card for each GPU with its power, temperature, VRAM and load; RAM; each disk with its maker's logo and the space used on it; the processes holding VRAM. Each measure is a graph of the last minute and a green bar of now, side by side;
  • Tools | Cobra torch settings (Settings | Tools | Cobra torch): what the System Monitor shows, graph, bar or both, how many cores and GPUs a line, and a Testing computer (2 AMD EPYC CPUs, 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, 2 Samsung SSDs) to see it with big hardware;
  • File | New | Conda Env File.
The conda commands run in a new Terminal tab, in the file's directory; on a remote computer, in the Run tool window.

The Anaconda, NVIDIA, Intel, AMD, disk makers' and package logos are trademarks of their respective owners and are shown only to identify the software. Cobra torch is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any of them.
